title: Word stats
intro: You are building a small text-analysis helper. Use only the standard library (no pandas). Each level extends the code from the previous one, so keep your functions.
rules: A word is a maximal run of letters or apostrophes, compared in lowercase. Everything else (spaces, digits, punctuation) separates words.
Ties are always broken alphabetically, so the output is deterministic.

levels.title: Count words in a text
levels.prompt: Write `count_words(text)` that returns a dict mapping each word to the number of times it appears. Keys must appear in the order the words first occur in the text.
levels.sampleInput:
text = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The dog barks; the quick brown fox runs away! A quick brown fox is a happy fox.'
print(count_words(text))

levels.title: Top k words ignoring stopwords
levels.prompt: Write `top_k(text, k, stopwords)` that returns the k most frequent words as a list of (word, count) tuples, ignoring every word in `stopwords`. Sort by count descending, then by word ascending. If fewer than k distinct words remain, return all of them.
levels.signature: def top_k(text: str, k: int, stopwords: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, int]]
levels.sampleInput:
text = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The dog barks; the quick brown fox runs away! A quick brown fox is a happy fox.'
stop = ['a', 'is', 'over', 'the', 'away']
print(top_k(text, 3, stop))

levels.title: Most common bigrams
levels.prompt: Write `top_bigrams(text, k, stopwords)`. First remove every stopword from the word sequence, then count each pair of neighbouring words that remains. Return the k most common bigrams as a list of ("word1 word2", count) tuples, sorted by count descending then by the bigram string ascending. The whole text is one sequence: sentence ends do not break a bigram.
levels.signature: def top_bigrams(text: str, k: int, stopwords: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, int]]
levels.sampleInput:
text = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The dog barks; the quick brown fox runs away! A quick brown fox is a happy fox.'
stop = ['a', 'is', 'over', 'the', 'away']
print(top_bigrams(text, 3, stop))
edgeCases: Fewer than two words left returns []
